la:verb:diligo.gloss: to esteem, prize, love, have regard, to delight in (something)
senses: to esteem, prize, love, have regard, to delight in (something)
to set apart by choosing, to single (something) out, to distinguish (something) by selecting it from among others
la:verb:diligo.html:
dī-lĭgo, lexi, lectum, 3, v. a.
2. lego
. Prop., to distinguish one by selecting him from others; hence, in gen.,
to value or esteem highly, to love (v. amo init., and cf. faveo, studeo, foveo, cupio; very freq. and class.).
Prop.: nihil est enim virtute amabilius, nihil quod magis alliciat ad diligendum: quippe cum propter virtutem et probitatem etiam eos, quos numquam vidimus, quodam modo diligamus,; cf. sq.; 14, 50; ; et saep. (cf. also the passages with diligo which are cited under amo, 1. and 1. colo, II. 2. b.); ; ; ; ; et saep.: satin habes, si feminarum nulla'st, quam aeque diligam?; cf. ; ; ; ; ; : te in germani fratris dilexi loco,; cf. ; : quem di diligunt, whom the gods favor, denoting a fortunate person, ; ; . —Prov.: diligitur nemo, nisi cui fortuna secunda est,.
Transf.
Of inanimate objects: fidem est complexus, observantiamque dilexit,; cf.: Caesaris consilia in re publica,: benevolentiam, diligentiam, prudentiam mirifice,: aviae memoriam,: auream mediocritatem,: Cypron, et saep. —
Very rarely, of inanimate subjects, to love, choose, affect: montes amant cedrus, larix, etc.... montes et valles diligit abies,—*
With inf. for amare, to do willingly or habitually, to be fond of doing: pira nasci tali solo maxime diligunt,.—Hence,
dī-lĭgens, entis, P. a., prop. esteeming, loving; hence, in respect to an inanimate object, careful, assiduous, attentive, diligent, accurate with regard to it, opp. negligens (very freq. and class.).
In gen.
With praepp.: qui in re adventitia atque hereditaria tam diligens, tam attentus esset,; so, in rebus omnibus, : in exquirendis temporibus,: in ostentis animadvertendis,: in compositione,: in philosophia,: in eloquendo,: in symmetria,: ad custodiendum aliquem diligentissimus,; so, ad reportandum,: ad cetera,: diligentes circa hoc,: circa aerarium,.—
With gen.: omnis officii diligentissimus,: veritatis,: imperii,: disciplinae,; cf.: litterarum veterum,: compositionis,: aliarum rerum quae vitam instruunt,: temperamenti,: naturae,attentively investigating it,; so, medicinae, et saep.—*
With dat.: Corinthios video publicis equis assignandis et alendis, orborum et viduarum tributis fuisse quondam diligentes,.—
Absol.: experientissimus ac diligentissimus orator,: pro cauto ac diligente, Caes. Fragm. ap. P.; for which: ut a diligenti curiosus distat,; cf. ; et saep.—
Transf., of inanimate subjects: assidua ac diligens scriptura,; cf.: diligentior notitia,: stilus,: remedia,; ; .—
In partic., with reference to domestic affairs, frugal, thrifty, economical (cf. its opp. negligens = prodigus, and Ruhnk. , a, ed. Frotsch.): homo frugi ac diligens, qui sua servare vellet,; ; cf. opp. negligens,; and c. c. parcus and opp. luxuriosus,: cum te pro illiberali diligentem (appelles),: ex re familiari, cujus diligentissimus erat,.—Hence, dīlĭgenter, adv. (acc. to II. A.), carefully, attentively, diligently: accurate agatur, docte et diligenter,; ; ; ; ; ; A. fin.; —Comp., ; ; ; ; —Sup., ; ; ; —
dīlectus, a, um, P. a., loved, beloved, dear (rare).—With dat.: pueri dilecti Superis,; so ; 8, 758.—In sup., ; .—Absol.: luce mihi carior dilectior fili,; —Subst.: dīlectus, i, m., = ὁ ἐρώμενος, a favorite, .

la:noun:diligentia.html:
dīlĭgentĭa, ae, f.
diligens
,
carefulness, attentiveness, earnestness, diligence (freq. and class.; cf.: labor, aerumna, opera, industria, assiduitas, sedulitas, studium, cura).
In gen.: reliqua sunt in cura, attentione animi, cogitatione, vigilantia, assiduitate, labore; complectar uno verbo, quo saepe jam usi sumus, diligentia, qua una virtute omnes virtutes reliquae continentur, (v. the whole chapter in connection).
With praepp.: pro mea summa in re publica diligentia,: in controversia,: in verbis,: diligentia tua in retractandis operibus,: circa proprietatem,: circa istum lacum, Traj. ap. : erga pecuniam alienam,: diligentiam adhibere ad rem,: in rem,; 16, 9, 4; cf. .—
Absol., ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; ; et saep.: obscura,; cf. inanis,: nimium sollicita,; : sinistra,—
Rarely with gen.: sacrorum, the care of, etc., ; cf.: dignitatis commoditatisque,: mandatorum tuorum,: tenuis illa divisionis,: nostri,i. e. affection for us,: Ecclesiae Dei,.—
In partic., carefulness in household affairs, i. e. economy, frugality, ; ; — Plur. (very rare): maritorum inefficaces diligentiae,precautions,.

la:verb:dilato.html:
dīlāto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a. and n.
differo
.
Act., to spread out, dilate; to enlarge, amplify, extend (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.).
Lit.: (stomachi) partes eae, quae sunt infra, dilatantur, quae autem supra, contrahuntur,: manum (opp. comprimere digitos),: globum farinae, Müll.: fundum,: castra, (opp. coartatio plurium): aciem,: cicatricem,: patulos rictus,: se mare, et saep.—
Trop.: ut aut ex verbis dilatetur, aut in verbum contrahatur oratio,; so, orationem,; cf. argumentum, id. Parad. prooem. § 2: haec, quae dilatantur a nobis, Zeno sic premebat,; cf. ; : eloquentia dilatata (opp. contracta et astricta),: litteras,to pronounce broadly,: nomen in continentibus terris, id. Fragm. ap. : quantis in angustiis vestra se gloria dilatari velit,; cf. se (c. c. attollere),: haec lex, dilatata in ordinem cunctum, coangustari etiam potest, —
Neutr., to extend one's self ( = expandor): spatia montis in cubiculo dilatantia, Sill. N. cr.

senses: to fall apart, disintegrate, break up
la:verb:dilabor.html:
dī-lābor, lapsus, 3,
v. dep. n., to fall asunder, go to pieces, melt away, dissolve (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: glacies liquefacta et dilapsa,; cf. nix,: nebula,: calor,: Vulcanus (i. e. ignis),: aestus, et saep.—Of a river, to flow apart, flow away, hoc quasi rostro finditur Fibrenus, et divisus aequaliter ... rapideque dilapsus cito in unum confluit, : amnis presso in solum alveo dilabitur,; cf. Mütz. ad h. 1.—Poet.: ungula in quinos dilapsa ungues,divided,: (Proteus) in aquas tenues dilapsus abibit,melting,.—
In partic.
In the historians, of persons, esp. of soldiers, to move away in different directions, to flee, escape, scatter, disperse: exercitus amisso duce brevi dilabitur,; so,absol.,; ; ; — With ab: ab signis,; cf. .—With ex or e, ; .— With in: in oppida,; cf. ; ; .—With ad, ; : domum,fin.: ab eo,desert,.—
Pregn., to tumble down, i. e. to fall to pieces, go to decay: monumenta virum dilapsa,; so of buildings, Drak.; ; ; fin. al.: navis putris vetustate,: supellex,: cadavera tabo,; cf.: corpora foeda,: fax in cineres, et saep.
Trop. (acc. to I. B. 2.), to go to decay, go to ruin, perish, be lost: male parta male dilabuntur, like our light come, light go, Poëta ap. (for which, disperire, ): ne omnia dilabantur, si unum aliquod effugerit,: praeclarissime constituta, respublica,: res familiaris,: divitiae, vis corporis, etc.,: res maxumae (opp. crescere),: omnis invidia,: tempus,i. e. to slip away,: vectigalia publica negligentiā,i. e. to fall into confusion,: curae inter nova gaudia,to vanish, et saep.: sunt alii plures fortasse, sed meā memoriā dilabuntur,vanish,.—
Of time, to glide away, pass: dilapso tempore,.

la:verb:diluo.html:
dī-lŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3,
v. a., to wash to pieces, wash away; to dissolve, dilute, cause to melt away; to wash, drench (freq. and class.).
Lit.
Ingen.: ne aqua lateres diluere posset, * : sata laeta boumque labores,; cf.: sanguine diluitur tellus, is soaked, Furius Antias ap. : unguenta lacrimis,: alvum helleboro,: vulnus cruris aceto,; cf.: ulcus ovi albore,: colorem,i. e. to wash out, weaken,; : amnes diluuntur,.—
In partic., to dissolve any thing in a liquid, i. e. to temper, dilute, mix: absinthia,; ; cf. venenum,: helleborum,: vinum,i. e. to dilute with water,; v. under P. a.: favos lacte et miti Baccho (i. e. vino),; cf.: Hymettia mella Falerno,: insignem bacam aceto,: medicamentum aceto,; ; : circaeam in vino,: rutam cum mero,: medicamentum ex aqua, et saep.
Trop.
To weaken, lessen, impair; to do away with, remove: adversariorum confirmatio diluitur aut infirmatur aut elevatur,: res leves infirmare ac diluere (opp. confirmare),; : molestias omnes (c. c. extenuare),; cf.: curam multo mero,: seriorem horam mero,: vitium ex animo (Bacchus), (4, 16, 6 M.): crimen,; ; ; (opp. obicere); 9, 2, 53 (c. c. negare) et saep.; cf. also ; ; ; et saep.: invidiam aliqua cavillatione,: injurias aere pauco,to atone for,: omnes affectuum vires, Quint, 11, 1, 52: ejus auctoritatem,: memoriam tam praeclarae rei,.—*
Analog. with its synon. dissolvere, to solve a difficulty, i. e. to explain: mi, quod rogavi, dilue,.—Hence,
